records.notes: Rule: "A constant-name, data-name, file-name, report-name, or screen-name described using a GLOBAL clause is a global name. All data-names subordinate to a global name are global names. All condition-names associated with a global name are global names." cite.py --check 13.18.27.4 "All data-names subordinate to a global name are global names. All condition-names associated with a global name are global names" -> OK §13.18.27.4 1). VERIFIED ARMS (probe g1b @0caa7d5, --std 2023): a GLOBAL constant (01 KG CONSTANT IS GLOBAL AS 7) reads 7 in a directly and an indirectly contained program; subordinates GA and GC OF GB OF G of `01 G GLOBAL` are read and written from both levels (writes visible in the container: BACK GA=ABC after INNER2's SET, GC=11); condition-name GA-ABC is tested (IF) and SET TO TRUE from contained programs; a GLOBAL FD's file-name is OPENed/WRITten in a containee and read back by the container (FILE=WROTE1); a file-section `01 NFR GLOBAL` under a non-GLOBAL FD is global (OUTER/INNER round-trip). BinderDriver.BindUnitData injects each ancestor's CallGlobalRoots subtree + its condition-names and adds DataBinder.GlobalBridgesOf bridges. Report-name GLOBAL has goldens conformance:85/pb369_global_report_use_selection; screen-name is the declined A.4.2 module (COBOLNET1560). DIVERGES — CRASH on legal source, two shapes (see findings): (1) a GLOBAL FD with TWO record descriptions plus ANY contained program (even one referencing nothing) fails the backend `CS0102: The type '_PRG_OUTF._PRG_INF' already contains a definition for '_redef_R1'` — both records are CallGlobalRoots of one StringCanonical redefines class and BinderDriver adds GlobalBridgesOf(g) per root with no de-duplication, so the shared `_redef_` backing bridge is emitted twice (same for `01 G GLOBAL` + `01 H REDEFINES G GLOBAL`, both data-names 'described using a GLOBAL clause'); (2) a GLOBAL clause on a redefiner whose class is not StringCanonical (`01 G PIC X(5) VALUE "HELLO". 01 G-RED REDEFINES G GLOBAL PIC X(5).`, containee DISPLAY G-RED) emits `private ref string G_RED => ref __outer.G_RED;` for a field the container never declares plus an un-bridged anchor reference -> CS1061 + CS0120. Both at 2002 and 2023 (85 lacks GOBACK in the probe; the shapes are 85-legal). Note the inventory's GR-13.18.27.4-3 CONFORMS ('B resolves') is contradicted by shape (2) on this tree. Related open notes (not this mechanism): kb/Work PB1243 (containee own subordinate vs container GLOBAL subordinate -> false ambiguity, GR2), PB1193 (record-level GLOBAL; its title premise no longer reproduces), PB1009 (landed, GLOBAL linkage bridge). No note owns the duplicate/phantom bridge — NEW finding. No spec-derived test pins GR1 (test-needed).

Rule: 'The New method allocates storage for an object, initializes its instance data in accordance with 14.6.2.4, Initial state of object data, and returns a reference to the created object.' (cite.py --check 16.2.1.2 -> OK §16.2.1.2 1)). §16.1 lets an implementation provide 'alternative root classes' (cite.py --check 16.1 'an implementation may provide alternative root classes' -> OK §16.1) and COBOL.NET's implicit root supplies a predefined NEW on every class: InvokeForm.New renders obj = new Class() (generated ctor chains base then VALUE-initializes), InvokeForm.NewSelf renders this.__New() for SELF|SUPER "NEW" in a factory (covariant, OoEmitter ~l.311/995), and class::"NEW" goes through OoBinder.InlineInvocation. VERIFIED (probe/new2.cob at --std 2002 and 2023): the returned reference is non-NULL; two NEWs yield independent storage (B1 mutated to 'XYZ 099', B2 still '--- 007'); object data takes its VALUE ('---', 007) and an OBJECT REFERENCE with no VALUE is NULL; pinned by conformance:2002/oo_instance_data (---/---/XYZ), oo_factory and pb428_inline_method_invocation exercise the NewSelf/inline forms. NOT VERIFIED / NOT REACHABLE: (1) the New of the standard BASE class itself - `CLASS-ID. X INHERITS FROM BASE` is refused COBOLNET0821 (re-probed probe/base1.cob at --std 2023), owned by kb/Work PB1506 (open; names this row as one its implementer claims); (2) the internal-file-connector and collating-sequence components of §14.6.2.4 for object data were not probed. Two halves, one verified -> PARTIAL. No new defect beyond PB1506.

Rule: 'If resources needed to create a new object are not available, the returned object reference is set to NULL, and the EC-OO-RESOURCE exception condition is set to exist and is propagated back to the runtime element that invoked the New method.' (cite.py --check 16.2.1.2 'the returned object reference is set to NULL, and the EC-OO-RESOURCE exception condition is set to exist' -> OK §16.2.1.2 2)). Code: EC-OO-RESOURCE exists only as a catalog entry (ExceptionCatalog.cs:171, L3 Fatal); grep over src finds NO raise site. NEW renders a bare C# `new Class()` / `__New() => new Class()` (BoundOo InvokeForm.New / OoEmitter ~l.314) with no OutOfMemoryException handler, so resource exhaustion escapes as an unhandled .NET exception instead of NULL + EC-OO-RESOURCE. The planned slice (docs/COBOLNET_OO_SLICE_BRIEFS.md l.248 'EC-OO (EC-OO-RESOURCE on New per §16.2.1 GR2 ...)') never landed. Contrast: CobolPtr.cs:211 already maps OutOfMemoryException to NULL + a condition for ALLOCATE - the precedent the fix should reuse. Not probed (resource exhaustion is not reproducible in a golden); decided by code reading. No kb/Work note owns EC-OO-RESOURCE (grep 'OO-RESOURCE' kb/Work -> none) - NEW finding, see findings.json 'ec-oo-resource-never-raised'. The BASE-class half is kb/Work PB1506's.

Rule: 'When invoked on an instance object, the FactoryObject method determines the class of the object and returns a reference to the factory object associated with that class.' (cite.py --check 16.2.2.2 -> OK §16.2.2.2 1)). The FactoryObject method belongs to BaseInterface (§16.2), the object interface of the standard BASE class, which is not provided: `INHERITS FROM BASE` is refused COBOLNET0821 (probe/base1.cob --std 2023), and no class carries a predefined FactoryObject - `INVOKE B1 "FactoryObject" RETURNING F1` (F1 USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE FACTORY OF BOX) is refused COBOLNET0825 'class BOX (and its inheritance chain) does not define an instance method named FactoryObject' at 2002/2014/2023 (probe/new1.cob). grep -ri FactoryObject over src/ and tests/ -> zero hits. The facility is absent -> NOT-IMPLEMENTED. Owning note: kb/Work PB1506 (open, MAJOR, rejects-legal-source: BASE / BaseFactoryInterface / BaseInterface absent; names GR-16.2.2.2-1 as a row its implementer claims) - cited, not re-reported. The planned slice docs/COBOLNET_OO_SLICE_BRIEFS.md l.248 ('§16.2.2 FactoryObject') never landed.

Rule: §4.2.10 'Nonstandard extensions are language elements or functionality in an implementation that consist of any of the following: 1) documented language elements not defined in this Working Draft International Standard;' (cite.py --check 4.2.10 'documented language elements not defined in this Working Draft International Standard' -> OK §4.2.10 1)). The class is definitional, but its obligations - 'Documentation associated with an implementation shall identify nonstandard extensions for which support is claimed' and 'An implementation shall provide a warning mechanism that optionally may be invoked by the user at compile time to indicate use of a nonstandard extension' (both cite.py OK §4.2.10 3), the catalog attaches them to GR-4.2.10-3) - are what make a class-1 element a CONFORMING extension, and neither holds. MEASURED on pinned 0caa7d5: probe/ext1.cob (PIC S9(5) COMP-3, PIC S9(5) COMP-5, COMP-2 - usages ISO defines at no edition) compiles and runs with ZERO diagnostics at --std 85 and --std 2023; `cobol --help` offers no extension-flagging option (only --permissive, which moves REMOVED ISO constructs, and --sign-encoding); the >>FLAG-02/-14 pass (FlagConformancePass) flags ISO migration items, not extensions; grep of src for a nonstandard-extension warning finds none. DOCUMENTATION: docs/CONFORMANCE.md names the vendor words only as RESERVED WORDS (D-RW1: CHANNEL, COMP-1..5, COMPUTATIONAL-1..5, END-INVOKE, ... pinned by CobolWordsDriftTests) and COMP-4 only as a synonym inside DOC-A.1-208; no section identifies which nonstandard extensions are CLAIMED (e.g. COMP-1/-2/-3/-5, END-INVOKE per PB758, order-free OPTIONS per PB1508, COLLATING-less SORT/MERGE per PB1139, qualifier/subscript interleaving per PB1455). Other extensions ARE refused by name (ENTRY and INSPECT ... TRAILING draw COBOLNET2269 - probe/ext2.cob, ext1 variant), which is conforming for those. Harm: silent - a user asking for portability has no way to learn that COMP-3 is not ISO. NEW mechanism finding 'no-4.2.10-extension-warning-or-register' (findings.json); the per-construct notes PB1139/PB1455/PB1508/PB755/PB756/PB758 each cite §4.2.10 for their own shape but none owns the absent mechanism.

Rule: 'language elements defined in this Working Draft International Standard for which different functionality is implemented, where that language element is not required for conformance to this Working Draft International Standard, and standard support for that element is not claimed by the implementor;' (cite.py --check 4.2.10 'and standard support for that element is not claimed by the implementor' -> OK §4.2.10 2)). Definitional class; its obligations are §4.2.10's documentation + warning paragraphs (GR-4.2.10-3). Members in this implementation = the ACCEPT-INERT declined elements (docs/CONFORMANCE.md §1/§4): SEND/RECEIVE (COBOLNET1578), COMMIT/ROLLBACK (1579, StatementBinder.BindCommitRollback), VALIDATE statement (1580), RECORD DELIMITER (1778, witness conformance:2023/pb292_record_delimiter_witness + the DocumentedNonSupportWitnessTests methods in test-ref) - each documented in CONFORMANCE §2/§4/§5 AND flagged by a named compile-time warning: VERIFIED by the doc rows and the witness. NOT MET for two members: (1) the OPTIONS FLOAT-DECIMAL clause (A.3 item 13, Not claimed) binds inert with NO warning (probe/fd.cob compiles clean at 2014/2023) - owned by kb/Work PB298 (Registrar-15d extension); (2) the EC-MCS-* exception-names are accepted against a facility with no setting sites, which CONFORMANCE §4 item 1 itself flags as owed - MCS witness debt, kb/Work PB1198/PB374. Most members verified, two not -> PARTIAL. No new mechanism beyond those notes (the general absence of an EXTENSION warning is reported under GR-4.2.10-1/-3).

Rule (four sentences, cite.py --check 4.2.10 each -> OK §4.2.10 3)): (a) class 3 - a REQUIRED element with different functionality is an extension only 'provided that standard-conforming behavior is also implemented and that an implementor-defined mechanism exists for selection of the nonstandard behavior'; (b) added reserved words are permitted; (c) 'Documentation associated with an implementation shall identify nonstandard extensions for which support is claimed and shall specify any reserved words added for nonstandard extensions'; (d) 'An implementation shall provide a warning mechanism that optionally may be invoked by the user at compile time to indicate use of a nonstandard extension in a compilation group. This warning mechanism shall flag only extensions that are syntactically distinguishable.' VERIFIED: (a) the selectable nonstandard behaviours have standard defaults and a CLI selector (--permissive accepts removed constructs WITH a warning; --sign-encoding ibm|ascii), src/Cobol.Net.Cli/Program.cs; (b)+(c)-reserved-words: docs/CONFORMANCE.md D-RW1 lists the 23 extension-reserved words, equal to cobol-words.json extensionReserved, pinned by CobolWordsDriftTests (the test-ref). NOT MET: (c)-extensions: no CONFORMANCE.md section identifies the nonstandard extensions for which support is claimed (COMP-1/-2/-3/-5, COMPUTATIONAL-n, END-INVOKE, the OPTIONS order-freedom, COLLATING-less SORT/MERGE, ...); (d): NO warning mechanism exists - probe/ext1.cob (COMP-3/COMP-5/COMP-2, syntactically distinguishable) compiles clean at --std 85 and 2023 with no option or directive that would flag it; FlagConformancePass implements >>FLAG-02/-14 migration flags (§7.3.14/15), a different obligation. Harm: silent. NEW mechanism finding 'no-4.2.10-extension-warning-or-register' (findings.json); related per-construct notes PB1139, PB1455, PB1508, PB755, PB756, PB758, PB396 cite §4.2.10 for their own shape only. Two of four sentences unmet -> DIVERGES.

Rule: 'When the term integer is used as a constraint for an operand in a general rule, that operand shall evaluate at runtime as follows: a) If native arithmetic is in effect, the implementor shall define when the operand represents an integer. b) If any mode of standard arithmetic is in effect, the operand shall be equal to a standard intermediate data item ... whose content has the unique value zero or whose decimal fixed-point representation contains only zeros to the right of the decimal point.' (cite.py --check 5.5 'the implementor shall define when the operand represents an integer' -> OK §5.5 3) a)). Editions: the arithmetic-mode split is ISO 2002+ (standard arithmetic introduced 2002). VERIFIED at the subscript general rule (§8.4.2.3.4 GR1b): probe/gr3b.cob with EC-ALL checking ON, subscript X/2 = 2.5 -> 'EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT (fatal): subscript value 2.500000000 is not an integer' under BOTH ARITHMETIC IS NATIVE and STANDARD-DECIMAL; under STANDARD-DECIMAL 1/3*3+65 evaluates to exactly 66 (SDIDI rounding) and is treated as an integer, consistent with b). Reference-modification has the same runtime test (CobolString.cs 'reference-modification position ... is not an integer'). NOT MET / UNVERIFIED: (1) a)'s 'implementor shall define' has NO documentation - Annex A.1 item 124 ('Native arithmetic (when an operand or arithmetic expression is an integer). ... shall be documented', (5.5, Integer operands)) has no DOC-A.1-124 row in docs/CONFORMANCE.md (that row, GAP, is separate from this one); the code's de-facto definition is 'the exact scaled Int128 value has a zero fraction'. (2) At intrinsic integer ARGUMENTS the runtime never applies the test: FUNCTION FACTORIAL(X / 2 + 1) (=3.5) prints 6 and FUNCTION CHAR(X / 2 + 64) (=66.5) returns ordinal 66, with EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION checking ON and FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS blank (probe/ch2.cob, gr3b.cob) - IntegerArgReal truncates (Math.Truncate) and the Int128 path narrows the fraction away. Whether §5.5 3) itself governs argument rules is contested (IntrinsicArgumentRules says §5.5 corroborates, §15.3 governs), so this is reported under §15.3 14) as NEW finding 'runtime-integer-argument-fraction-truncated' (sibling of open kb/Work PB617's static half). One site class verified, documentation and a second site class not -> PARTIAL.

Rule: "The GLOBAL clause may be specified only in the following entries: a) A constant entry. b) A data description entry whose level-number is 1 that is specified in the file, working-storage, local-storage, or linkage section. c) A screen-description entry whose level-number is 1. d) A file description entry. e) A report description entry." cite.py --check 13.18.27.3 "A data description entry whose level-number is 1 that is specified in the file, working-storage, local-storage, or linkage section" -> OK §13.18.27.3 1) b); twin cite.py --check 13.16.3 "The CONSTANT RECORD and GLOBAL clauses may be specified only in data description entries whose level-number is 1" -> OK §13.16.3 6). Code: DataBinder.ClausePlacement row (DataClauseKind.Global, Residence, '§13.16.3 SR6 / §13.18.27.3 SR1 b)', EntrySections.All) -> COBOLNET2404. PROBES @0caa7d5. ADMITTED (compile + run clean): `01 K CONSTANT IS GLOBAL AS 5` and `1 K2 CONSTANT GLOBAL AS 'AB'` (a) at 2023 (constant entry is 2002+, COBOLNET0900 at 85); `01 ... GLOBAL` in FILE (incl. under an SD, and `1 W GLOBAL`), WORKING-STORAGE, LOCAL-STORAGE, LINKAGE (b) at 2002/2023; `FD F IS GLOBAL` (d); `RD RPT IS GLOBAL` (e); `01 T TYPEDEF GLOBAL` (a level-1 data description entry; §13.18.58.4 GR3). REFUSED: `77 X77 PIC X GLOBAL` and `05 X05 PIC X GLOBAL` -> COBOLNET2404 at 85 and 2023; `88 ... GLOBAL` -> COBOLNET1747; `66 R66 RENAMES A GLOBAL` -> COBOL0307; report group `01 RG TYPE DETAIL GLOBAL` -> COBOL0307; `SD S GLOBAL` (an SD is not a file description entry; §13.4.6.2 prints no GLOBAL) -> COBOL0307. Arm c) is the declined screen module (docs/CONFORMANCE.md#A.4.2 Not claimed): `01 SG GLOBAL` in a SCREEN SECTION -> COBOLNET1560 (witness a42-screen-global), which A.4.1 makes the conforming posture. kb/Work PB1045 (open) claims this row but its own 2026-09-24 addendum records the SR1 arms refused COBOLNET2404 (PB518) and its open part is the SR4 arm (SR-13.18.27.3-4, not this row).

Rule: "If the GLOBAL clause is not specified in the file description entry of a containing program, the file shall not be referenced directly or indirectly by any input-output statements in any contained program, unless they are defined as external files in each of the source elements in which they are referenced." cite.py --check 13.18.27.3 "the file shall not be referenced directly or indirectly by any input-output statements in any contained program" -> OK §13.18.27.3 3). PROBES @0caa7d5 (--std 2023; 85/2002 identical on the WRITE shape). DIRECT: containee `READ F` / `CLOSE F` / `WRITE R` against a non-GLOBAL FD -> COBOLNET1639 'not defined' (the file-name and a non-global record are simply not visible — correct outcome). EXTERNAL exception: container and containee each declare `FD F IS EXTERNAL`; containee WRITE -> container reads back EXTRN (allowed, correct). INDIRECT (the arm the rule exists for): a record `01 R GLOBAL` under a non-GLOBAL FD is legitimately visible in the containee (§13.18.27.3 SR1 b); a containee MOVE to it compiles and runs), and a containee `WRITE R` / `REWRITE R` is refused — but ONLY through §14.9.51.3 SR5 / §14.9.35.3 SR1 (COBOLNET1757: "'R' is not a logical record of any file description entry"), a false reason for this program: R IS a logical record of FD F. There is no mechanism of this rule's own; the refusal is an accident of StatementValidation.ResolveRecordName/FileWhoseRecordIs looking only at the containee's own FDs. The outcome is right on every shape probed, the diagnosis is not and is not durable — PARTIAL. Owning note kb/Work PB1193 (open): its body names SR-13.18.27.3-3 and owes the dedicated check (record visible via its own GLOBAL, FD not GLOBAL -> refuse under the containee I-O rule), not re-reported. No spec-derived test (test-needed).

Rule: 'When the term integer is used as a constraint for an operand in a syntax rule, then a) if that operand is a literal, it shall be an integer literal, as defined in 8.3.3.3.2 ...; b) if ... a data-name or an identifier, it shall reference ... 1. an integer intrinsic function, 2. a fixed-point numeric data item, other than an intrinsic function, whose description does not include any digit positions to the right of the radix point.' (cite.py --check 5.5 'an integer intrinsic function' -> OK §5.5 2) b) 1.). ONE primitive: PicInfo.IsIntegerDescription = IsClassNumericFixedPoint && Scale <= 0, consumed through the OperandPositions register and the per-binder screens. PROBED on pinned 0caa7d5 at the SR sites that write 'integer': PERFORM ... TIMES (§14.9.28.3 SR2 'Identifier-1 shall be an integer'): PIC 9V9 -> COBOLNET1646, COMP-2 -> 1646, PIC PP9 (digits right of the radix via P) -> 1646, FUNCTION NUMVAL("2") (numeric, not integer function) -> 1646, literal 2.0 -> rejected (parse), while PIC 9 / PIC 9PP (P-scaled integer, ran 200 times) / FUNCTION INTEGER(2.5) are admitted - all three arms a), b)1., b)2. and the P-scaling edge; identical at --std 85 (probe/int3.cob). STOP RUN WITH NORMAL STATUS 2.5 -> COBOLNET1704 citing §14.9.42.3 SR3 (literal arm). OCCURS DEPENDING ON PIC 9V9 -> COBOLNET0852 (§13.18.38.3 SR17); GO TO DEPENDING ON PIC 9V9 -> COBOLNET2324 (§14.9.17.3 SR1). The test-refs pin the PERFORM item arm and the status literal arm. Note: intrinsic ARGUMENT rules are not SR sites (§15.3 governs them; IntrinsicArgumentRules' own comment); their static-screen gaps are PB617's and the new finding under GR-5.5-3. || REFUTED: PARTIAL - the rule governs EVERY syntax rule that constrains an operand by 'integer', and one such site does not enforce it: §8.8.2 rule 5 'The second operand shall be an integer operand' (cite.py --check 8.8.2 -> OK §8.8.2 5)). Probed on pinned 0caa7d5 --std 2023 (refute-probe/shift.cob, shiftl.cob): COMPUTE BC = BB B-SHIFT-L D with D PIC 9V9 and COMPUTE BC = BB B-SHIFT-L 1.5 both compile clean and run (1.5 silently truncated via RescaleEscape to 1); arms a) and b)2. escape. ConditionBinder.BindBoolShiftSuffix binds the count as an unrestricted arithmeticExpression without the IsIntegerDescription screen; already owned by open kb/Work PB1413 (SR-8.8.2-5). The other sites the refuter re-probed hold: SET identifier-1 PIC 9V9 -> COBOLNET2326 (§14.9.39.3 SR1), SEARCH VARYING PIC 9V9 -> COBOLNET2325, STRING/UNSTRING POINTER and TALLYING -> COBOLNET1651, GOBACK WITH NORMAL STATUS 2.5 -> COBOLNET1704. The test-refs exist and pin the PERFORM TIMES and status-literal arms only.
